item.title: Seahawks sign Trevon Diggs, Bobby Hart to 53-man roster
item.description: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Seahawks sign Trevon Diggs, Bobby Hart to 53-man roster appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks are coming out of a bye , preparing for a Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. With several players on the IR, or just dealing with injuries, it appears the club decided to bring Trevon Diggs and Bobby Hart to the team. Reports indicate that both Diggs and Hart were added to the Seahawks’ 53-man roster on Monday , according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Diggs provides some solid depth to the cornerback room, while Hart does the same for the right tackle position. “The Seahawks signed cornerback Trevon Diggs and tackle Bobby Hart to the 53-man roster,” Rapoport reported. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Diggs was at one point considered a top player in the secondary. In his second year in the league with the Dallas Cowboys, he led the NFL with 11 interceptions and two picks returned for touchdowns. However, since his departure from the franchise in the middle of the 2025-26 campaign, things haven’t quite been the same for the 28-year-old. Trevon Diggs has already made five appearances for the Seahawks this season, but his production has been minimal. The seven-year veteran enters Week 12 with just one tackle. As for Hart, the 32-year-old offensive lineman has been a journeyman in the league throughout his 10 years in the league. The Seahawks are the sixth team he’s played for, as he’s played in two games for Seattle so far this year. He’ll have a chance at earning some playing time against the 49ers in Week 12. Either way, the club is seeking its seventh win of the season. But it will be a tough task, as the Seahawks travel south to take on the 49ers on the road. item.title: Todd Golden’s Boogie Fland update suggests shoulder injury hasn’t gone anywhere
item.description: Candice Ward-Imagn Images Todd Golden’s Boogie Fland update suggests shoulder injury hasn’t gone anywhere appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Florida Gators regrouped this past week, getting back in the win column after defeating West Virginia, following their first loss of the season at the Players’ Era Tournament against Houston . The Gators have a home game this week on Tuesday against Milwaukee, but they will be short-handed in the lineup again. Junior guard Boogie Fland, who is dealing with a shoulder injury, was ruled out Florida’s game against Milwaukee, as per Jon Rothstein of 247Sports. The latest update on Boogie Fland’s injury came from Florida head coach Todd Golden. Fland initially sustained the injury back on Nov. 11 during the Gators’ win against Florida State. He missed a game, but then returned for the Players’ Era Tournament. Fland then re-aggravated the injury during Florida’s matchup against Notre Dame, but was still in the lineup for the Houston loss. Fland missed the Gators’ win against West Virginia, and will now miss a second consecutive game. He was expected to be a major impact player for Florida this season as one of the team’s starting guards. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Fland has played in five games this season for the Gators, at a little over 24 minutes per game. He has been averaging 6.8 points, 2.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.4 steals with splits of 41.7 percent shooting from the field, 42.9 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 57.9 percent shooting from the free-throw line. He is in his second season with the Gators after beginning his college career at Arkansas. He had a strong freshman year with the Razorbacks, before entering the transfer portal and committing to Florida. item.title: BYU Overcomes 15-Point Deficit, Beats Washington in Maui
item.description: LAHAINIA, HI- NOVEMBER 23: Jaxon Kohler #0 of the BYU Cougars takes a shot in the first half during a first round Southwest Maui Invitational college basketball game against the Washington Huskies at the Lahaina Civic Center on November 23, 2026 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images BYU fell behind by 15 points in the first half, but defense, hustle, and key shot making from Collin Chandler carried BYU in a 83-77 win over Washington in the first round of the Maui Invitational. With no Rob Wright as he deals with a leg ailment, BYU was disoriented on both ends of the floor early on. BYU got a spark off the bench from Brooks Bahr, whose defense and hustle slowed down UW and created second chance opportunities. BYU shot a miserable 22-36 from the foul line, but had 18 second chance points compared to 9 for UW. Some of these key second chance points came after missed free throws. Collin Chandler carried the scoring load, leading BYU with 24 points on 3-6 three-point shooting and 9-10 from the FT line. Jaxon Kohler had three first half fouls and picked up his fourth in the first 90 seconds of the second half, but still finished with 15 points in just 18 minutes. Tyler Betsey scored 13 points and Bruce Branch added 10. Bruce was a paltry 4-12 from the foul line, but had some key rebounds and had 3 blocks. BYU faces a stiffer test tomorrow when they play an undefeated Ole Miss team who leads the nation in defensive turnover percentage. The game tips off at 12:30 MT on ESPN2.

item.title: Close friend of ESPN, Broncos icon Tom Jackson shares details surrounding ‘unexpected’ death
item.description: When NFL fans rolled out of bed on Sunday morning to turn on ESPN’s NFL Sunday Countdown , viewers were left heartbroken and stunned to learn of the sudden death of Tom Jackson . Jackson’s longtime ESPN partner Chris Berman shared the news to start the show, which came as a shock. An official cause of death has not been revealed, but ex-Denver Broncos linebacker Bob Swenson, who was a close friend of Jackson, revealed some details of what Jackson was going through in the weeks leading up to his passing. MORE: Broncos’ Sean Payton gives heartwarming gesture to Tom Jackson’s family after death Swenson spoke with the Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson and revealed Jackson was considering back surgery and had other issues in the days leading up to his death. Oct 21, 1984; Orchard Park, NY, USA; FILE PHOTO; Denver Broncos linebacker (57) Tom Jackson on the bench against the Buffalo Bills at Rich Stadium. Denver defeated Buffalo 37-7. Mandatory Credit: Mandatory Credit: Tony Tomsic-USA TODAY NETWORK © Tony Tomsic Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) “I talked to him every week, sometimes every day,” Swenson said. “I talked to him and he was going back and forth about getting a back operation and then he said he was going to do it. Then I texted him but I wasn’t getting a response the last couple of days. “I texted him November 10. I would send him stuff and he came back and said, ‘That’s funny.’ I won’t say what the joke was. He just said he was going to do the back surgery and he had some things going on with his leg. I was just waiting to hear back [about the surgery]. I texted him, ‘Are you OK?’ I think I texted him on Thursday and Friday and no response. I was just stunned [at learning of his death].” MORE: ESPN ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ revives ‘Jacked Up’ segment to honor Tom Jackson Remembering Tom Jackson Sep 14, 2015; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson smiles prior to the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Atlanta Falcons at the Georgia Dome. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-USA TODAY Sports Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Before becoming a household name on ESPN, Jackson was a vaunted defender and member of the Broncos’ “Orange Crush” defense. As a player, Jackson was a fourth-round pick in 1973 out of Louisville, before becoming a two-time Pro Bowl during his 14 years with the Broncos. As an analyst, he was once again among the best, becoming a Hall of Fame broadcaster. Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 after his final assignment, the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony alongside Berman. Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan. Our deepest condolences go out to Jackson’s family and friends during this incredibly difficult and tragic time. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: 2028 three-star IOL Lance Ciechanowski commits to Texas
item.description: The Texas Longhorns landed the third pledge of the 2028 class on Monday when Chatsworth (Calif.) Sierra Canyon interior offensive lineman Lance Ciechanowski committed to head coach Steve Sarkisian and position coach Kyle Flood. View this post on Instagram The 6’5, 290-pounder picked up his offer from Texas in June 2025 after a strong camp performance on the Forty Acres. The other offers for the big Californian are Arizona State, Cal, Colorado State, Kansas, Minnesota, Ole Miss, Purdue, Sacramento State, and UCLA with the Sun Devils hosting Ciechanowski a year ago for an unofficial visit. Also a shot putter in high school, Ciechanowski is a consensus three-star prospect ranked as the No. 526 player nationally and the No. 44 interior offensive lineman in the 247Sports Composite rankings. For Flood, Ciechanowski doesn’t quite represent the typical “big human” mold, but considering the movement issues encountered by offensive lineman he’s recruited who arrived carrying significant mass, taking a big-framed lineman the staff can mold into their preferred weight might actually benefit the program. View Link Ciechanowski joins Plantation (Fla.) American Heritage quarterback Neimann Lawrence and Spring Klein Oak running back Micah Rhodes in the 2028 recruiting class for the Longhorns.

item.description: ATHENS, GA - OCTOBER 04: Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann of the Georgia Bulldogs looks on prior to the college football game between the Kentucky Wildcats and the Georgia Bulldogs on October 04, 2025, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Florida State has made official the worst-kept secret in coaching carousel news, announcing that Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann will be the next head coach of the Seminoles. Schumann spent the last three seasons (four including the current one) at the helm of the UGA defense after serving as co-coordinator with current Oregon head coach Dan Lanning. In that time the Red and Black have finished 1st, 7th, 2nd, and now 1st again in scoring defense. Schumann served as a graduate assistant under Kirby Smart and Nick Saban at Alabama before coming to Athens, and was among the staff Smart was most eager to bring with him.At the time some even referred to Schumann as Smart’s ““secret weapon.” That might be overstating things a bit, because Smart knows a thing or two about defenses himself and Schumann’s contributions in Tuscaloosa weren’t that secretive. They certainly aren’t now, as he’s helped develop the Bulldog defense into a perennial standout, and has grown into one of the game’s premier in-game coaches. Georgia’s second half defensive adjustments under Schumanns have been remarkable at times. Schu will stay in Athens through the playoffs while beginning work on his staff and recruiting for the Noles. That’s certainly not ideal, but announcing the move now was probably the best of the bad options for Kirby. It allows Georgia to get the news out and move on before the playoffs. My sense is also that Kirby has known this was coming for a few days, and is likely already well into his search for a replacement. Given that three of the four men who have held the DC job under him have become Power 2 head coaches (the other is Will Muschamp, who’d already been on that ride), the Bulldog job will draw interest from all corners of the country. Congrats to Coach Schumann on a well-earned promotion. Now let’s go swat some Yellow Jackwts. Go ‘Dawgs!!!

At the time, the brief exchange seemed like an unexpected acknowledgment of a developing college football coaching rumor. However, less than 48 hours later, Beamer’s words suddenly carried considerably more significance. And what initially appeared to be an innocent conversation between former colleagues now looks remarkably well-timed. Beamer’s Saturday night message takes on new meaning Following Georgia’s victory at Williams-Brice Stadium, Beamer approached Bulldogs defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann during the customary postgame exchanges. The two coaches, who previously worked together at Georgia, shared a brief conversation. However, Beamer’s message went beyond congratulating his former colleague. “I hope that FSU thing works out if that’s what you want,” Beamer told Schumann. The exchange was captured in footage shared by FOX Carolina News and subsequently circulated across social media. At the time, Schumann had emerged as a leading candidate for Florida State’s vacant head coaching position. item.title: Patriots Could Reunite With Former Tom Brady Weapon After A.J. Brown Injury
item.description: Patriots Could Reunite With Former Tom Brady Weapon After A.J. Brown Injury originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Patriots ' offensive situation has been one of the bleaker in all of the NFL. For a Patriots team that was hoping to be among the league's best offensive squads this year, especially with newly acquired wide receiver A.J. Brown, that clearly hasn't been the case. There are many reasons as to why, and Brown has been a significant part of that. Multiple players have been released over the past couple of days, allowing the Patriots to take a chance on guys who might still have something left in the tank. One of them is a former New England player who once was with the Patriots when Tom Brady was their quarterback. That guy is none other than Brandin Cooks, who played with New England back in 2017. “The 49ers announced a couple of roster moves ahead of Sunday’s game against the Vikings in Mexico City. Veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks has been waived to make room on the active roster for defensive lineman C.J. West. West was activated from injured reserve on Saturday,” Josh Alper wrote . The idea of bringing in Cooks isn't the wrong one, but again, being 33 years old and certainly well past what he was back in the day is something that has to be considered. Cooks is still a respectable veteran and, at the very least, could be a guy who brings something to this offense. Cooks hasn't really gotten much playing time since the 2023 season with the Dallas Cowboys, when he played in 16 games and caught 54 passes for 657 yards. item.title: North Carolina reportedly lands 5-star forward CJ Rosser, giving Michael Malone nation's top 2 prospects in his first recruiting cycle
item.description: The results on the court in Michael Malone's first year as North Carolina's head coach have so far been mixed. But he's crushing it on the recruiting trail. Per multiple reports i ncluding from On3's Joe Tipton , five-star forward CJ Rosser committed to North Carolina on Monday. An athletic, 6-10 forward, Rosser is a two-way player and a capable 3-point shooter. He's the No. 2 prospect in the Class of 2027, according to Rivals. North Carolina secured the commitment of No. 1 prospect DeMarcus Henry (small forward) last week, giving the Tar Heels the top two prospects in the Class of '27, per Rivals , and the nation's No. 1 ranked class as of Monday. Among others, North Carolina also has offers out to No. 4 overall prospect Beckham Black (point guard) and No. 16 overall prospect Nasir Anderson (point guard). Rosser also received offers from Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan and Louisville, among others. Michael Malone's decision to hire Chuck Martin from John Calipari and Arkansas is paying off. Ryan Hunt via Getty Images Malone hired John Calipari's recruiting coordinator Malone took over at North Carolina in the offseason to replace Hubert Davis, a UNC alumnus and former player who struggled to maintain the program's lofty standards in his five years as head coach. Malone joined North Carolina as a virtual NBA lifer and the first head coach without ties to the program since Frank McGuire took the reins in 1952. He previously coached the Denver Nuggets to eight winning seasons out of 10 and the franchise's first NBA championship in 2023. But his arrival came with questions about his ability to adjust to college basketball after spending his previous 22 seasons coaching in the NBA. He gave himself an early leg up. Malone's first staff hire was to lure Chuck Martin away from Arkansas as his associate head coach. Martin was John Calipari's recruiting coordinator at Arkansas and during his latter years at Kentucky in addition to working as an assistant under Calipari at Memphis. He also worked for Malone when Malone was the head coach at Manhattan from 1999-2000. The hiring is already paying dividends for Malone and North Carolina. On the court, the Tar Heels are off to a 4-1 start without having yet played a top 25 opponent. Their loss arrived at home to unranked Georgia on Nov. 13. They have upcoming non-conference games against Arkansas and Kentucky among others before getting into the heart of their ACC slate.

item.title: 3 Massive Takeaways From A Thrilling Night Of Muay Thai Action At The Inner Circle 39
item.description: Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium lit up as The Inner Circle 39 delivered five electric Muay Thai wars, capped by two thunderous quarterfinal firefights that confirmed the final four of the blockbuster 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix . The card streamed exclusively for members at live.onefc.com in Asia primetime on Friday, November 20, and the intensity never dipped for a single second. A World Champion retained his crown, an unbeaten star kept rolling, and the road to the final just got more intriguing. Here are three massive takeaways from a night that had everything. Imangazaliev Showed Why He Is The Man To Beat Photo Credit: ONE Championship Reigning ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Asadula “The Dagestan Ninja” Imangazaliev has a gift for finding a way, and he found one yet again in the main event. Facing #1-ranked contender Aslamjon “El Pantera” Ortikov for the second time in five months, the undefeated Russian slugger took another split decision and retained his crown for the first time. Rematches are unforgiving. The mystery is gone, the hiding places are gone, and every habit, weapon, and rhythm is on film. Ortikov knew all of it, and he still could not break the code despite having his moments. item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Neville, Keane and Manchester United meltdowns at world’s funniest comedy club
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Hoo-boy. Short of forgetting to put on his washable virgin wool navy trousers before striding towards the visitors’ dugout at Anfield, it’s difficult to imagine how Mauricio Pochettino’s spell in charge of Manchester United could have got off to a more humiliating start. Having witnessed his new team go a man and two goals down in less time than it takes to listen to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven twice, it was a rendition of Sacked In The Morning that could be heard from the home fans inside 15 minutes. Poch would later complain that the decision to dismiss Leny Yoro was questionable, but it was far less baffling than his own call to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in a year after almost 12 months out with knack. Across 90 harrowing minutes, the Dutch defender didn’t so much look off the pace as resemble a confused tourist who’d wandered on to the pitch while trying to find his way to the stadium museum. In a footballing world obsessed with micro-marginal-gains – think custom-weighted laces, aerodynamic socks, or nice calming shades of green for training ground walls – how about one modest proposal that otherwise does my nut in? That a multimillion pound player, paid hundred of thousands each week, has to walk all the way around the pitch with ligament injuries . Carry him, give him crutches, or put him in a wheelchair! Is it just me? It has a very 1950s amateur air of ‘dont make a fuss, ‘tis a mere scratch’” – John Williams. Since he was such a good friend to Mauricio Pochettino in his previous role, can we assume Donald Trump will be ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card once he’s finished his morning nap?” – Declan Hackett. If Mikel Arteta is correct in his assertion that “ We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League ” how does he explain his team’s Micky Mouse defending for Newcastle’s second goal at St James’ Park on Sunday?” – Dominic Hodgson. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
